sources.name: BLS · Principal Federal Economic Indicators
sources.why: Primary statistical releases with methods, tables, and revision practices.
sources.caveat: Survey estimates and seasonal adjustments are not direct counts; revisions matter.

sources.name: BEA · Economic Accounts Releases
sources.why: Primary national, industry, regional, and international economic accounts.
sources.caveat: Modeling, imputations, benchmark revisions, and later vintages can materially change estimates.

sources.name: EIA · New Data and Products
sources.why: Recurring energy surveys, administrative series, and documented statistical products.
sources.caveat: The feed mixes releases with analytical products; each linked methodology controls.

sources.name: EIA · Today in Energy
sources.why: Short analysis tied closely to identifiable EIA data.
sources.caveat: This is analysis, not the underlying statistical release.

sources.name: Federal Reserve Board · Releases
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why: Direct statements, orders, policy actions, and enforcement releases from the institution.
sources.caveat: A statement establishes what the Board announced, not the truth of every underlying representation.

sources.name: Federal Reserve · H.4.1 Balance Sheet
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why: A recurring statement of Federal Reserve balance-sheet positions.
sources.caveat: Accounting categories are defined by the release and do not by themselves explain causal effects.

sources.name: Federal Reserve · H.8 Commercial Banks
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why: Recurring estimates of assets and liabilities of U.S. commercial banks.
sources.caveat: The release contains estimates, seasonal adjustments, and later revisions.

sources.name: Federal Reserve · Senior Loan Officer Survey
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why: Structured reports from bank lending officers on standards, terms, and demand.
sources.caveat: Respondent judgments are systematically collected but remain reported perceptions.

sources.name: Federal Register · Significant Documents
sources.why: Structured metadata and links for officially published rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents.
sources.caveat: FederalRegister.gov is an unofficial presentation; each item links to the official edition and source material.

sources.name: GAO · Reports and Testimony
sources.why: Audits, program evaluations, legal decisions, and testimony with disclosed institutional authorship.
sources.caveat: Findings depend on scope, access, sampling, and agency responses stated in each report.

sources.name: CBO · Publications
sources.why: Budget estimates, cost estimates, projections, and methodological working papers.
sources.caveat: Outputs are conditional estimates and projections, not observations of future outcomes.

sources.name: CDC · Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.why: Timely public-health surveillance, investigations, and official recommendations with methods and source citations.
sources.caveat: MMWR is the agency voice and includes recommendations; surveillance findings and policy guidance should not be conflated.

sources.name: Supreme Court · Slip Opinions
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
sources.why: Official slip opinions and the Court's own syllabus metadata.
sources.caveat: An opinion establishes the Court's disposition and reasoning; it does not make every recited historical assertion independently true.

sources.name: New York Court of Appeals · Decisions
sources.publisher: New York State Law Reporting Bureau
sources.why: Official state reporter feed for New York's highest court.
sources.caveat: The court currently places an anti-bot screen in front of some automated requests; failures are reported rather than silently substituted.

sources.name: New York Appellate Division · First Department
sources.publisher: New York State Law Reporting Bureau
sources.why: Official state reporter feed covering Manhattan and the Bronx appellate department.
sources.caveat: The court currently places an anti-bot screen in front of some automated requests; failures are reported rather than silently substituted.

sources.name: New York Commercial Division · Selected Decisions
sources.publisher: New York State Law Reporting Bureau
sources.why: Official selection of trial-level commercial decisions.
sources.caveat: This is a selected set, not all Commercial Division decisions; selection criteria can shape coverage.

sources.name: How Appealing · Appellate Links
sources.why: A secondary legal pointer that routinely links to opinions, filings, and the reporting it summarizes.
sources.caveat: Selection and headlines are editorial. Follow the link to the opinion or filing before treating a proposition as adjudged.

sources.name: CourtListener · Opinions and RECAP
sources.why: Open opinions, oral arguments, alerts, and federal docket documents with stable identifiers and direct document access.
sources.caveat: Coverage varies by court and record type; RECAP depends on document acquisition from PACER and participating users.

sources.name: SEC · EDGAR Filings and Data
sources.why: Primary company filings, exhibits, XBRL facts, and filing metadata.
sources.caveat: A filing establishes what was submitted. Audited financial statements, unaudited figures, and management narrative have different evidentiary weight.

sources.name: Treasury · Fiscal Data
sources.why: Machine-readable debt, revenue, spending, interest, and cash-management records.
sources.caveat: Series definitions, accounting periods, and later corrections control interpretation.

sources.name: FRED · Series and Vintages
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.why: A convenient distribution layer that preserves release vintages for many official series.
sources.caveat: FRED is often a distributor rather than the originating statistical agency; use source notes and vintage dates.

sources.name: NCHS · National Health Statistics
sources.why: Vital statistics, surveys, methods, and recurring health data products.
sources.caveat: Provisional and final data differ; suppression, weighting, and reporting lags matter.

sources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov · Study Records
sources.why: Structured registrations, protocol fields, status changes, and submitted results.
sources.caveat: Registration is a party submission, not independent verification; missing or delayed results are informative.

sources.name: OpenAlex · Scholarly Works
sources.why: Open scholarly metadata suitable for stable author-identity monitoring.
sources.caveat: Metadata can be incomplete or misattributed; an author identifier is stronger than name search.

sources.name: Crossref · Retraction Watch Data
sources.why: Structured notices of retractions and other post-publication changes.
sources.caveat: Retraction categories and publisher notices require reading; a retraction is not a universal finding of misconduct.

sources.name: World Bank · Development Indicators API
sources.why: Documented cross-country series with source and methodological metadata.
sources.caveat: Comparability, national statistical capacity, revisions, and missingness vary substantially.

sources.name: UN Comtrade · Trade Records
sources.why: Officially reported bilateral merchandise and services trade data.
sources.caveat: Mirror statistics diverge; classifications, valuation, timing, and reporting quality vary.

sources.name: UCDP · Candidate Events
sources.why: Systematic, geocoded, event-level conflict coding with explicit definitions.
sources.caveat: Candidate data are provisional and constrained by source visibility and coding rules.

sources.name: SIPRI · Arms and Military Expenditure
sources.why: Long-running, methodologically documented datasets on arms transfers, spending, and forces.
sources.caveat: Opacity in defense sectors requires estimation; trend-indicator values are not transaction prices.

sources.name: ADP · National Employment Report
sources.why: Estimates derived from a large payroll-processing system rather than respondent recollection.
sources.caveat: ADP customers are not the entire labor market; proprietary transformations and benchmark choices matter.

sources.name: Indeed Hiring Lab · Data Portal
sources.why: High-frequency operational data on postings and job-search activity.
sources.caveat: The platform's market share, customer mix, duplicate postings, and product changes affect representativeness.

sources.name: Redfin · Housing Data Center
sources.why: Timely listing and transaction data with published definitions and downloadable series.
sources.caveat: Multiple-listing-service coverage and revisions vary by geography; listings are not completed transactions.

sources.name: Bank of America Institute · Consumer Checkpoint
sources.why: Aggregated card and deposit-account activity provides direct operational evidence about participating customers.
sources.caveat: The customer base is selected; published notes combine telemetry with institutional interpretation.

sources.name: JPMorganChase Institute · Household and Business Data
sources.why: De-identified transaction and account records support analysis of cash flow, balances, and firm behavior.
sources.caveat: Customer selection and proprietary cleaning limit population inference; the analysis remains interested-party research.

sources.name: Cloudflare Radar · Internet Traffic
sources.why: Operational network telemetry can reveal outages, traffic shifts, protocols, and attacks.
sources.caveat: Visibility is bounded by Cloudflare's network and customer mix; classification methods can change.

sources.name: Carta · Data Desk
sources.why: Operational cap-table and fundraising data illuminate private-company financing and ownership.
sources.caveat: Carta clients are a selected subset of private firms; product strategy can shape publication choices.

sources.name: Pew Research Center · Datasets and Methods
sources.why: Survey datasets, questionnaires, sampling descriptions, and methodological reports.
sources.caveat: Prefer the instrument, topline, and microdata to article framing; nonresponse and question wording matter.

sources.name: RAND · Research Reports
sources.why: Often substantial methods, models, datasets, and institutional review.
sources.caveat: Commissioning, assumptions, and policy objectives matter; keep commentary separate from empirical appendices.

sources.name: Foreign Affairs
sources.why: Useful high-level synthesis and informed argument about international affairs.
sources.caveat: It belongs on an interpretation shelf, not in the measurement stream.

sources.name: Brookings · Research
sources.why: Policy analysis with identifiable authors, data, and institutional programs.
sources.caveat: Research and advocacy are intermingled; the underlying data and assumptions deserve separate inspection.

sources.name: Nature Podcast
sources.why: Interviews and reporting tied to newly published scientific work.
sources.caveat: Journalism and editorial selection are not substitutes for the paper, data, or subsequent replication.

sources.name: The Naked Scientists
sources.why: Accessible interviews with scientists and discussion of current findings.
sources.caveat: It is an independent production, not an institutional publication of the University of Cambridge.
